request.system: You are a strict claim verifier. You only trust the catalog facts given to you.
request.user:
Verify every factual claim in the campaign is grounded in the catalog facts. Fail if any claim is unsupported, exaggerated, or contradicts the facts.
Rules (from reviewer overrides):
- ANY mention of an out-of-stock product (stock 0) fails, whether or not the copy prompts purchase — no editorial exception.
- Numeric spec claims (lumens, hours, capacity, ratings) must match the catalog exactly; doubling or inflating a spec fails.
- Transferring an attribute from another product, or upgrading 'water-resistant' to 'waterproof', is a fabricated claim and fails.
- A comparative or superlative claim ('brightest', 'longest-lasting', 'most X') is scoped to the product type named in the claim and checked against the comparison set below: it fails if a same-type peer beats the subject on the compared attribute. Vague puffery ('great gear', 'toughest', 'best ever') with no measurable attribute is acceptable.

Body: Hey,

You already know how to read a topo and pack a bear canister. This isn't that kind of email.

This is the other stuff — the habits that keep trails enjoyable for everyone who comes after you. A quick read before your next outing doesn't hurt.

---

YIELD ORDER

Uphill hikers have the right of way over downhill hikers. Horses and pack animals take priority over everyone on foot. Mountain bikers yield to hikers. When in doubt, step to the uphill side of the trail, make yourself visible, and let the other party pass.

---

STAY ON THE TREAD

Stepping off-trail to pass someone widens the trail over time and damages vegetation. If the tread is wide enough, pass with a nod. If it isn't, wait for a natural pullout — a rock, a clearing — before moving around.

---

SOUND

Keep music and calls to one earbud or use a low-volume speaker only in areas without other users nearby. In a canyon or tight corridor, sound carries further than you expect. Announce yourself with a calm "on your left" well before you reach another party — not at the last second.

---

CAMPSITE DISTANCE

Most land management agencies ask for 200 feet (roughly 70 adult paces) between your camp and water sources, trails, and other parties. That distance protects riparian areas and gives everyone a buffer of quiet.

---

WASTE

Pack out what you pack in. Human waste in high-use or fragile areas should go in a WAG bag. Where catholes are appropriate, dig 6–8 inches deep and 200 feet from water. Toilet paper, even "biodegradable," packs out.

---

FIRE

Check current conditions before you build a fire — not just the general fire danger rating, but the specific rules for the area you're in. Conditions change mid-trip. A fire ring doesn't mean fires are currently permitted.

---

SAY HELLO

A nod or a simple "morning" to passing hikers costs nothing. On quieter trails it's also a safety measure — mutual acknowledgment means someone noticed you were there.

---

None of this is complicated. Most of it is just paying attention to what's around you, which you're probably already doing.

See you out there.

— The Northbay Supply Team
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.
